scope: Design review only; no live storage implementation or CPU measurements
conclusion: Allocate an Arc array and explicitly construct each final slot during scatter. Do not assign into unconstructed elements or alter vector internals.

sources.title: C++23 draft N4950, allocator.members and specialized.construct
facts: allocator<T>::allocate(n) creates the array object and returns its initial-element pointer; element lifetimes are not started.
construct_at performs placement construction from its forwarded arguments.
deallocate must receive the original allocation pointer and allocation count, not the current logical size.

sources.title: C++23 draft N4950, basic.life
facts: Storage reuse or release can end a class object's lifetime without calling its destructor.
Only constructed slots may be read. A span is exposed after all slots have been constructed.

sources.title: WG21 P0593R6, section 5.10
facts: The array-lifetime rule was introduced to support container storage and array pointer arithmetic independently of element construction.
The design does not rely on pair being an implicit-lifetime or trivially-copyable type.

sources.title: WG21 P0784R7, specialized.construct
facts: construct_at was added in C++20 and is specified through placement construction.

required_invariants: Use size_t for logical size and capacity; let allocator handle size and alignment checks.
Restrict raw storage to trivial weights, trivial Arc destruction and non-throwing Arc construction from an endpoint and weight; preserve vector fallback for other weights.
Every scatter destination occurs exactly once and is within the allocated array.
Construct with construct_at(data + index, to, weight); do not read a slot before construction.
Copy only the constructed logical range, using object construction rather than memcpy of pair.
Move transfers pointer, allocation count and logical size together, then resets the source to empty.
A rebuild preserves capacity when sufficient; growth allocates before releasing the old block.
Trivial destruction permits clear without scanning slots; retained slots are reconstructed before later use.
Producer or allocation failure still invokes the graph's existing clear_edges path.
Prefetch computes an address within the allocated Arc array and never reads an unconstructed object.
rejected_shortcuts: Assigning through an allocator pointer without starting element lifetimes
Using a union Slot array as span<Arc>
Changing vector's private size or treating capacity as initialized elements
